objective: Improve peak timing and peak size against FluSight-ensemble on matched archived-report forecast tasks.

deadline.policy: Stop launching experiments before the deadline; reserve the last 30 minutes for scoring and final synthesis. Preserve already-running fits and disclose unfinished work.

comparison.training: For each held-out season, retrain the sampled MLP on the other three seasons among 2022-23 through 2025-26. Current training inputs are finalized admissions and flu-ED histories; prediction labels are 36 future weekly values of both series.
comparison.evaluation: Replay archived Wednesday reports with no finalized fallback, including observed weeks of the peak window. Final NHSN admissions supply peak labels over epiweeks 40-21. Match location/reference-date cells to FluSight-ensemble in 2024-25 and 2025-26; require observed past-window reports.
comparison.scope: Retrospective development comparison, not an untouched or forward-only validation. States/DC, reference dates at or before the true peak. Actual weeks to peak may define diagnostics, never forecast-time decisions.
comparison.metrics: Peak-week negative log probability with floor 0.001; peak-size WIS on log(1+admissions). Lower is better. Report both metrics, by season and early/near-peak; disclose any coverage change.

rounds.change: Add differentiable negative log probability of the true future peak week; weights 0.3 and 1, retaining existing weekly, path and peak losses. Retrain both candidates; seeds 44 and 45.
rounds.decision: No aggregate gain over original four-seed model; weight 1 is dominated by weight 0.3 overall. Keep original parent; retain weight 0.3 only as an uncertain parent because it improves 2025-26 timing. Test annual-calendar removal on both; do not declare a win based on one season.

rounds.change: Retrain on archived reports or synthetic report errors instead of finalized histories; keep weekly prediction labels finalized and original path/peak losses. Separate branch from added peak-week log loss.
rounds.decision: Archived-report training is worse on timing and size than the original four-seed model in both evaluated seasons; do not expand it. Synthetic reporting errors yield only a small aggregate timing improvement (3.316448 vs 3.336325), with worse size (0.352320 vs 0.305119), and near-peak timing worsens even though early timing improves. This two-seed screen does not establish a better recipe or an ensemble win. Retain original as parent pending calendar and shape branches; artificial errors remain a secondary option for a later combination only if independent improvements justify it.

rounds.change: Remove annual-calendar feature; retain all other training inputs, labels and respective losses. Retrain with seeds 44 and 45.
rounds.decision: Removing calendar without added peak-log loss improves aggregate timing and size, but gains come from 2024-25 and early forecasts; 2025-26 and near-peak timing worsen. Retain as provisional alternative parent, not confirmed winner, and do not expand solely on aggregate. Calendar removal plus peak-log0.3 has much worse size. Wait for shape and loss ablations before selecting a combination or seed confirmation; no ensemble timing win.

rounds.change: Add causal multiscale shape features; compare unsmoothed and smoothed summaries. Training inputs, labels, and losses remain original. Distinct hypothesis while reporting and calendar branches finish.
rounds.decision: Unsmoothed features improve size both seasons, timing aggregate and both lead groups, but timing slightly worse in2025-26. Best new aggregate candidate; test two combinations, not a confirmed ensemble win. Smoothed features lose to unsmoothed in both metrics/seasons; drop smoothing.

rounds.change: Remove peak loss; alternatively remove both peak and path losses. Test whether auxiliary objectives help before adding seasonal alignment complexity. All training inputs and weekly labels unchanged.
rounds.decision: Removing peak or both peak/path losses worsens both aggregate metrics. Retain auxiliary losses; do not expand ablations. Window-alignment hypothesis not disproved, but simple removal is harmful.

rounds.change: Combine unsmoothed features with calendar removal or artificial reporting errors; distinct training-input interventions; original labels/losses unchanged.
rounds.decision: Shape with artificial errors improves timing in both seasons and both lead groups versus original, and aggregate size, though2025-26 size marginally worse. Confirm with seeds46/47. Versus shape alone, timing/size tradeoffs remain. Calendar removal with shape hurts overall; drop it. No ensemble timing win.

rounds.change: Add seeds46/47 only to completed unsmoothed shape candidate; retain completed seeds44/45 and smoothing screen; no duplicate fits.
rounds.decision: Four-seed pooled shape model retains aggregate gains versus original four-seed model: timing3.132852 vs3.336325, size0.279492 vs0.305119. Size improves both seasons; timing2025-26 remains worse3.084169 vs3.024138. Early timing advantage over ensemble seen in two-seed screen disappears (2.911537 vs2.847819). Retain as confirmed aggregate improvement, not uniform improvement and not an ensemble timing win. Await artificial-shape confirmation before choosing next parent.

rounds.change: Compare6week and20week input context to12week parent, motivated by persistent near-peak timing deficit. No claim about which is better before results.
rounds.decision: Six-week history improves timing both seasons vs original and12week shape; size worsens overall vs shape, so not a universal improvement. Twenty weeks harms size badly; drop. Screen artificial errors with6/8week context; no ensemble timing win.

rounds.change: Confirm artificial-reporting plus shape candidate by adding only seeds46/47; keep completed44/45.
rounds.decision: Four-seed artificial shape retains timing and small size gains in both seasons vs original4seed, but aggregate3.174624/0.301929 is worse than finalized-input shape4seed3.132852/0.279492. Earlier two-seed estimate3.033872/0.288469 was optimistic. Artificial shape helps25-26 and near-peak timing relative to finalized shape, so retain as complementary candidate; no clear overall superiority or ensemble timing win. Await short-reporting screen before next confirmation.

rounds.change: Artificial reporting errors with6week or8week histories, unchanged final labels/losses.
rounds.decision: Eight-week artificial shape improves timing both seasons and both lead groups vs original; aggregate2.877616/0.295819 best timing so far, still worse ensemble2.578072. Size slightly worse25-26 vs original. Confirm with seeds46/47; prior artificial-shape optimism shrank with extra seeds. Six-week artificial is weaker, do not expand.

rounds.change: Confirm timing gains in both seasons with two additional seeds46/47. No new settings; preserve size tradeoff and compare four-seed results.
rounds.decision: Four-seed six-week multiscale model confirms timing gain both seasons: aggregate2.920574/0.299187 vs original3.336325/0.305119. Size improves both seasons, barely24-25; early8+ size0.355865 slightly worse original0.347608. Early timing2.574428 beats ensemble2.847819, but near3.011291 loses ensemble2.507377; no overall ensemble timing win. Retain as strongest confirmed timing parent; await eight-week artificial confirmation and capacity screen, avoid unnecessary late expansion.

rounds.change: Separate narrower-width96 child and distinct latest-two-permitted-training-seasons child; finalized admissions+ED histories,36 weekly labels, unchanged losses, seeds44/45. Motivated by six-week timing improvement in both seasons with size tradeoff.
rounds.decision: Do not expand either. narrow96 timing2.900588 has negligible aggregate advantage over4seed six-week parent2.920574 but size0.346791 worsens both seasons vs parent; latest2 is worse overall3.461390/0.357121. No ensemble timing win.

rounds.change: Confirm eight-week artificial-input shape timing improvement in both seasons with seeds46/47; reuse completed44/45. Preserve size25-26 tradeoff.

Eight-week finalized-history vs half-strength artificial-error training; separate history length and augmentation contributions. Unchanged36 future labels, losses, three permitted training seasons; two seeds44/45. Final focused screen before synthesis.

search_rules: Expand up to two promising parents per round, with a few small changes and one distinct idea; keep the parent as a matched-task reference.
Screen with two seeds where practical; confirm promising improvements with more seeds. Do not compare differing training budgets without identifying them.
Prefer repeatable timing gains across both seasons while retaining the size advantage. Drop consistently harmful children; record both scores and seed coverage for each decision.

Candidate branches include timing loss, reporting-revision robustness, season-aligned peak objectives, and simple out-of-fold calibration or mixtures. Select calibration using training folds only; never use the evaluated season or its true lead-to-peak.
Never blend in the reference ensemble just to manufacture a benchmark win.
Use one planner and seasonal scorer, pinned code snapshots, available patron GPUs, and exact manager plan/launch/status/rank commands. Keep completed caches out of docs.
Continue automatically when results arrive. Do not duplicate active jobs or repin their code. Stop new rounds early enough to summarize at 8 a.m. Eastern.

ili_complete.inputs_and_labels: ILI-converted admissions, leave one of ten 2011-12 through 2021-22 seasons out, excluding 2020-21; train on other nine; four seeds. Conversion calibrated on paired ILI/NHSN 2022-23 through 2025-26.

next_round_consideration: Collect eight-week artificial-input confirmation and six-week capacity/recency screen; prioritize complete scoring before11:30UTC synthesis. Four-seed six-week multiscale has repeatable timing gains both seasons, but no overall timing win over FluSight. No added timing loss, smoothing,20week history, or auxiliary-loss removal expansion.

objective_alignment_audit.training: dataset/cv.py masks out non-permitted seasons and creates origins throughout permitted epiweek31-30 seasons. Training path/peak losses use every available positive horizon, up to36, rather than evaluation epiweek40-21. Neighboring permitted seasons may supply future labels across a season boundary.
objective_alignment_audit.evaluation: seasonal.py constructs epiweek40-21 paths and includes already observed reported history before extracting the peak.
objective_alignment_audit.early_stopping: Inner validation scores only hidden validation weeks; peak_log_scores currently selects the maximum among those observed labels, which need not be the complete seasonal peak.
objective_alignment_audit.possible_experiment: Separate the peak-objective calendar mask from unchanged weekly labels and restrict auxiliary peak loss to an origin-specific epiweek40-21 window. Do not use any held-out timing information. Include scientific alignment checks if implemented.
